sensors.name: light sensor LLIGHT (dim under a tunnel roof)

control_flow: avoidWalls: if LLIGHT is below 70 (dim): if LEFT sees something turn left 20°, else if RIGHT sees something turn right 20°, else driveInTheDark; else (bright): driveInTheDark.
driveInTheDark: if LLIGHT is below 70: drive forward at 30 %; else stopAtWall.
stopAtWall: if FRONT sees something: stop; else followLine.
followLine: if the line tracker sees black: curve left; else curve right.

likely_intent.description: In a dark tunnel, turn away from a wall that comes close on the left or on the right, so the robot gets through a bending tunnel without touching it.

decision_points.condition: the left light sensor reads below 70 % (dim: inside a tunnel)

bright light: it goes to driveInTheDark

scenarios.coded_response: On a wall in front of its left half it turns left 20°, on one in front of its right half it turns right 20°, each time towards the wall; with neither it drives forward at 30 %.
scenarios.initial_condition: In dim light, inside a tunnel whose straight part has nothing in front of the robot and which bends to the right (left wall comes in front of its left half) or to the left (right wall comes in front of its right half) further on.
scenarios.trigger: The robot drives forward in the dark and comes to the bend, where a wall is in front of its left half (or its right half).
scenarios.title: Gets through a bending tunnel in the dark
assumptions: Getting through the tunnel means it drives on while nothing is in front of it.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It turns right when a wall is close on its left and left when one is close on its right, and so gets through the bend without touching the tunnel.

scenarios.coded_response: It follows the line, curving left on black and right otherwise, and stops when the front obstacle sensor sees the wall.
scenarios.initial_condition: In bright light, on a black line, with a wall across the line ahead.
scenarios.trigger: The robot follows the line towards the wall.
scenarios.title: In bright light, follows a line and stops at a wall

uncertainties: You said to turn right when a wall is close on the left, but your program turns left there, and it turns right when a wall is close on the right.
Your sentence doesn't say what the robot should do in bright light: there your program follows a line and stops at a wall.
In the dark your program drives forward without watching the front sensor, so a wall straight across the tunnel would not stop it.
Under a tunnel roof the light only falls below 70 % 7.5 cm inside, so a robot coming in from the light still drives as in the light for those first centimetres.
